articles.title: Ocarina of Time Is More Than a Nostalgia Trip – It Proves Nintendo’s Family Friendly Days Are Still Going Strong
articles.summary: Ocarina of Time revisits Nintendo's past in multiple ways, echoing not just its N64 origins, but the wonderful family-focused era of the Wii, which celebrates its 20th anniversary this week.
articles.body:
This is an opinion piece from writer Jess Kinghorn. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.

Even on the cusp of GTA 6's record-breaking train pulling out from the station, there's still another locomotive daring to take to the tracks. The Ocarina of Time remake is the criminal sandbox’s polar opposite, and its already broken Switch 2 sales records . It's easy to see why because it's just the latest success sprouting from the platform holder's tried and true strategy – and with the 20th anniversary of the Nintendo Wii on GTA 6 day no less, November 19, those magic beans continue to flourish. Games can be for everyone.

The Switch 2 is humble hardware compared to its console competitors, though The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is no less pretty. As I venture back into the Kokiri forest, witnessing its eternally childlike denizens come to terms with the passing of the Great Deku Tree and stare down the first autumn they’ve ever known, this fairytale has its hooks in me once more. It's what Nintendo is best at, and just goes to show that the studio completely understands how to pitch its family friendly games in a way no other platform holder has successfully managed to leverage.

Exceptions are few and far between. I loved Astro Bot , but that mascot platformer feels like an anomaly on the PlayStation 5. As for Xbox, I’m still a bit nervy about the fate of Banjo Kazooie maker Rare in the platform holder’s hands. The heaviest hitters on either console are more geared towards chasing greater graphical fidelity and technical fire power in order to impress the grown ups ( with a memory supply crisis price to match ). Nintendo has picked a distinctly different path, and it's not as if the Switch 2 is its first time stepping up to the plate.

While Ocarina of Time hails from the N64, and Nintendo’s family friendly approach dates back even further, it's really the humble Wii that set the publisher up for its modern success , ditching HD trends to instead focus on affordable gaming that truly had something for everybody. Rather than chasing the dragon of high fidelity graphics, first-party Nintendo releases focussed on strong art direction, with a case in point being WarioWare: Smooth Moves .

Released a few months after the Wii’s release, this rapidfire series of motion controlled minigames leveraged a blend of 2D and 3D art as its own easy to understand shorthand. Though 3D graphics are used sparingly, their sometimes rough and ready look only adds to the game’s humour. All of that silliness softens the blow of biffing a minigame with a sensible chuckle – precision picking Wario’s nose may be downright juvenile, but I’m no less charmed.

2008’s Animal Crossing: City Folk is less silly, but is similarly playful in its presentation. For instance, the village here looks a bit like Nintendo raided the craft box full of the really fun, patterned paper. While I appreciate New Horizons’ shininess, its strong art direction also makes the most of what the humble Switch 2 hardware has to offer.

Though everything is more expensive these days, I still feel Nintendo trying to resist that pull with the Switch 2. There's also something to be said for how, say, the Ocarina of Time remake sits on the minimal home screen like a doorway to adventure. Conversely, booting up my PS5 or Xbox Series X confronts me with an advertising upsell gauntlet. The Switch 2’s presentation is just one more cue borrowed from the Wii and its charming channel-based UI.

The clue to the Wii's success really is in the name, though a bigger giveaway would be the game library. Wii Sports launched as a pack-in title, offering a series of simplistic minigames to get a broad audience up to speed with its motion controls, while also stoking more than a little healthy competition in living rooms across the globe. Trust me, you’ve not lived until you’ve gone toe to toe at tennis with your Granny after one wine too many during Christmas dinner – those Wiimotes wrist straps really were non-optional.

And if Granny didn’t feel up to defending her tennis title but still wanted to enjoy a spot of seasonal family bonding, there were plenty of other options besides. For instance, 2007’s Super Mario Galaxy is the console at its toyetic best, offering an inviting experience that’s both fun to play as well as watch . There’s plenty of whimsy for all, with the platforming’s gravity effects entertaining players and onlookers alike, though using the motion controls to sniff out collectibles could easily become a group activity too.

Turn the Wii’s controller on its side, however, and New Super Mario Bros. Wii plays with a limited button layout just like the classic 8-bit adventure. With the Joy-Con 2, the more things have changed the more they stay the same.

Link also made an appearance in the Wii’s 21-strong launch line-up with The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess , another game that feels like it was still delivering on that ‘something for everyone’ promise, even as it skewed a bit edgier with its T for Teen rating. For me, it hit at just the right time and now I have the dynamic duo of Link and Midna to thank for my life long love of both werewolves and goth women. And despite not even being a co-op game, I have fond memories of playing it alongside (and arguing with) my baby sister.

Besides, what's easier to understand than waggling to swing a sword? Simplicity of play is a feature not a bug, and it's why going from Ocarina of Time to Twilight Princess to Breath of the Wild back to Ocarina of Time through the remake feels so natural. They've never had much crust to cut in the first place.

It's not as if mature games don't make an appearance on Nintendo consoles. Smart third-party exclusive deals such as No More Heroes or MadWorld on the Wii aren't a stone's throw away from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 finally gracing Switch 2 .

Nintendo’s first-party games, though, continue the Wii’s welcoming ethos. In a world where Fortnite and Roblox are filled to the brim with microtransactions, Nintendo's commitment to delivering worlds that anyone can enjoy simply as they are is refreshing. Whether I'm click-clacking across Switch 2 games, or dusting off the old Wii, remarkably little has changed – like Link pulling out that Master Sword, those 20 years have passed in the blink of an eye.

Jess Kinghorn is a freelancer writer who has written for PC Gamer, PLAY, and GamesRadar+.

articles.title: I’ve Played GTA 6 for 110 Hours, Here Are the Weirdest Things I’ve Seen
articles.summary: From a robot sex freak to a rebellious furry, these are the seven weirdest strangers I've met in GTA 6.
articles.body:
Warning: Spoilers for some of GTA 6’s open-world stranger encounters follow.

Just like Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 6 takes on a more mature tone compared to many of Rockstar’s prior games when it comes to its main story. But just like the studio’s western epic, there’s still plenty of room for the weird and wild when it comes to the people you’ll meet in its open world. I’ve spent over 110 hours driving, running, and sailing around the state of Leonida, getting myself into my fair share of unexpected situations along the way. From rebellious furries and naked adulterers to creepy sex robots and paranormal encounters, here are the seven craziest things I’ve seen so far in GTA 6.

Don’t worry, no story spoilers here! But if you’re worried about open-world surprises being revealed, then you should probably stop reading now.

GTA 6 is a very horny game when it chooses to be, and sometimes that has nothing to do with the hot couple at its heart. Things can and will get naughty when you least expect it. After a nighttime race through the freeways of Vice City, I took a stroll around the corner from the finish line at the Decor District car park. Walking along with Jason’s phone in hand, ready to “WaiNK it” (see: scan for vehicle details and security measures) at a nearby parked car to see if it could become my ride home, a light emanating from beneath a mostly closed garage door caught my attention. Little did I know what awaited me inside: a slice of AI-powered erotic horror.

The whole ordeal didn’t last long, but involved several partially built sex robots with oversized features and the kind of cartoonish eyes that burrow into the soul. There was no sign of the workshop’s owner, just me and its ungodly creations waiting to jump-scare me if I got too close. I made my way to the exit as quickly as I could, evading lunging limbs and dildos where hands should be, as dual-wielding mechanised humans urged me to stay and play. I left never to return, scarred from my run-in with Vice City’s thirstiest robots. Head over to near the bus stop on NE 17th Street if you don’t believe me. Assuming it’s in the same place for you, that is.

It’s not just robots, but also the humans of Leonida who can’t help but get up to no good. I was driving along a downtown Vice City street one day when, all of a sudden, a completely naked man ran out of a building asking for help. Before I had a moment to take in everything flopping around in front of me, I made the decision to see where this would take me and offered him a ride. What I thought would be a simple drive to his plush home turned into a chase ending with a moral dilemma.

Halfway through our journey, the woman he had just spent the night with and ran away from began her pursuit. Thankfully, it didn’t take long to shake them off, and we resumed the drive home. As we pulled up, though, I had the unfortunate experience of having to hear him pull an egg-shaped toy out of his rectum before leaving the purple and white plastic plaything on the driveway of his house. I was then presented with an option: be an honorable person and tell his wife the truth about what he was getting up to, or accept his bribe of one of the game’s 34 collectable watches and lie to her. I’ll let you decide which path I took.

From pork swords to beef slaps. One, singular Beefslap, to be precise. Beefslap was a simple yet kind soul I met by the side of the road in Northern Leonida, whom I still don’t know the legal name of. Wanting to be reunited with his friends at the Mud Club race track, but with no vehicle of his own to take him there, I duly offered a ride. This is a fairly simple one, but it ended in me having to throw a football as hard as I could into his nether regions in a Jackass-like test of strength. I guess this is what they do for fun here in Leonida.

Back in the city, and if there’s anything Grand Theft Auto loves to do, it's deliver cutting satire of the capitalist world we live in. Perhaps the best example of this I’ve found so far in GTA 6 is an encounter I had with a man who had just been involved in a car crash with a Sahara van — the in-universe parody of Amazon. Naturally, I pulled over to help the man and drag him out of the burning wreckage. I didn’t imagine that he’d then decide to crawl straight back into the flames, though.

You see, this scheming local saw the opportunity to cash in big time and sue the corporation whose driver had plowed into him. To make his case convincing, he made sure the burns on his body were sufficiently scarring as to squeeze as many dollars out of the situation as possible. He then offered me the opportunity to back him up in court over the claim and earn a chunk of the compensation myself. GTA 6 is all about making money, so of course I took the deal and found $12,500 deposited into my account some days later. And do I feel bad about lying on the record in order to rinse Amazo… I mean, Sahara of its pocket change? Absolutely not.

It isn’t just on the roads that people will bother you in Leonida, but on its many rivers, swamps, and stretches of ocean. One afternoon I was peacefully enjoying a spot of fishing out at sea by Washington Beach, and all of a sudden a boat pulled up next to me with its lone occupant offering conversation. After rudely commenting on my rudimentary rod and lure loadout, he offered me a test of his new hi-tech gear that will apparently revolutionise the angling world: the Finbuster.

Of course, faced with a possibility of a peek into the future, I accepted, promptly lobbing the round device into the water below. Turns out the Finbuster is essentially just a grenade, as a small explosion caused dozens of fish to float to the surface. You can’t deny its effectiveness, even if it does fly in the face of what should be a relaxing, patient activity. The real problem, though, is that not only did aquatic life fall victim to it, but human life, too. Two scuba divers rose and bobbed to the surface, looking very much dead. Naturally, police boats quickly made their way to the scene. Rather than helping out our new friend, I did the honorable thing and sped away as fast as I could. I’ve never seen him again. I wish him all the luck in his venture, though. Perhaps try Shark Tank?

It’s no secret that Rockstar loves a bit of Michael Mann. The director’s work, including Heat, Thief, and Miami Vice, can be seen throughout GTA 6 as well as earlier games in the series. If you’ve seen another of his movies, Collateral, you’ll know it centers on a hitman played by Tom Cruise who rides as a very pushy passenger with Jamie Foxx’s taxi driver, forcing him to drive around town. This happened to me in Vice City.

Upon switching to Lucia one day, a man in a suit just hopped into my car as I sat waiting at a red light. He then swiftly pulled a gun to my head and told me to do exactly as he said. If I tried to leave the car, he’d force me back into my seat, getting increasingly agitated. Out of curiosity, I had to see where he wanted to go. After a few minutes of following his directions, we arrived at the back of a small industrial building, and he told me to drive away and forget he ever existed. Instead, I waited as he walked through the door of his destination. Soon, I heard gunfire from within. Making my move, I walked inside only to find a drug operation, fresh bodies strewn across the floor. I fancied a bit of the powdered treasure for myself, so I decided to shoot the suited man and steal $11,000 worth of cocaine. A job well done.

Sometimes it isn’t all about the money, though. Sometimes it’s about fighting for freedom. I can’t say I expected that to be the case when I first spotted a man in full fox costume holding his paws in the air under a police spotlight, but the streets of Vice City often lead to unexpected places. Being the helpful citizen I am, I offered the vulpine in need an escape route – he hopped in my car and escaping the cops became priority number one. Luckily, he had a plan, and I quickly realised I had become part of something much larger.

Following his directions, I sped into a multi-story car park, switched vehicles, and he joined one of his furry friends in the back of a van as I took the driver’s seat. Little did I know that Vice City has enforced “No Paws Laws”, meaning furries are vulnerable to a shoot-on-sight policy from law enforcement. I smuggled my new friends back to their hideout on the lavish Starfish Island and got a look at their quite advanced setup, featuring plans and weapons for their startup liberation force. It wasn’t my place to join in the fight with them, though. That would just feel disingenuous. Instead, I drove away and listened to a Weazel News report of our escapades instead. “Pervert Alert,” the host proclaimed. I can only assume they were talking about the furries and not me.

Of course, there are plenty, plenty more peculiar strangers to meet and bizarre situations for you to get yourself into in GTA 6. Some are even complete optional questlines, which we’ll get further into over the coming days and weeks. What’s the weirdest thing you’ve seen in GTA 6 so far? Let us know in the comments.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: These Piranha Plant Slippers Double as Mario-themed Decor When You Put Them Away
articles.body:
Slippers are one of those classic Christmas gifts pretty much everyone has received at some point in their lives. They are one of those practical items that everyone is going to use at some point, but rarely do people actually get excited when they unwrap a new pair of slippers. Sure, there are plenty of themed options out there that feel fun, but where do you even put those when you aren't using them?

Well, if it's a pair of Piranha Plant slippers, that problem has been solved for you. Just place them back in their Pipe holder and your footwear is instantly transformed into a little Piranha Plant. Suddenly you've got a fun piece of Super Mario-themed decor that brightens up the space.

The Piranha Plant slippers are getting discounted as part of Amazon's Black Friday sale , dropping the price down to about $20. The deal is only available for Amazon Prime Members, but the typical price is still pretty cheap as far as Nintendo-themed gifts go. They are sold by a third-party seller, but the Amazon reviews are overall quite positive.

The main thing to note before you buy these slippers is that there is only one size available. It's a bit hidden in the product listing, but the page states that they are designed to fit for women with a shoe size ranging from 6-9 or men's shoe size beween 5-8 in the US. So if you're someone with bigger feet, you're probably going to have trouble actually wearing these things around the house.

And while adults can certainly wear these, they seem like an ideal gift for kids. If they had these in my size I would absolutely grab a pair at this price. I would have loved getting these as a kid too, but I don't think these even existed when my feet were still that small. Still, I'm definitely considering picking up a pair for my nephew who has fairly recently discovered Mario games for the first time.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: In GTA 6, Cars Are Way, Way More Than Just Getaway Wheels
articles.summary: GTA has always been obsessed with cars, but in GTA 6 your wheels are for more than just getaways - they're your mobile base.
articles.body:
The clue's in the name: Grand Theft Auto is a series obsessed with cars. Stealing them, racing them, modding them, escaping the police in them, bopping your head to their iconic radio stations, and sitting in the passenger seat conversing with colourful NPCs as you drive between missions.

But even in this petrolheaded company, GTA 6 stands out.

I'm not talking about the sheer variety of vehicles , from mobility scooters to muscle cars, nor the distinct grunts of its engines and whirr of superchargers, or even its expanded customization that tweaks everything from the upholstery to the transmission. It goes way beyond that: in GTA 6, your car is a mobile base, an extension of your character that sits at the centre of GTA's revamped and reworked systems. Without a car – specifically, without an owned car, rather than one nicked from the side of the street – I'm naked.

First, your car is the only way to manage all the guns you'll need.

In GTA 6, you physically carry weapons rather than hiding them in magically deep pockets. You can only wield two "longarms" – think rifles and shotguns – at a time, one on your back and one in a hand, and realistically you'll only want to carry one at a time because double-parking guns makes the no-nonsense cops twitchy.

Thankfully the trunk of your car can carry extra weapons (sneaking up to cop cars and jimmying the boot can get you a fresh gun in a pinch). Owned vehicles carry all your purchased weapons at once and you can switch them at will. Whenever I'm planning anything remotely violent, such as the lucrative gang hideout robberies, I take my owned vehicle so I'm prepared for anything.

Second, cars hold stashes of pilfered contraband.

Drugs, marked bills, jewellery: anything you steal worth a damn in GTA 6 is stuffed in a bag slung across your shoulder, and selling it through fences is a reliable way to accrue cash. Like with guns, you can only carry as many bags as you have arms. Your car becomes your pack mule, able to stack several stash bags at once so you can steal in sprees, rather than having to sell after every job.

Again, your owned vehicle is better because it'll retain your stash bags indefinitely, and between sessions. You can hit a drug den, head home to sleep, finish a few missions, quit the game, boot it up again hours later and your stash bag will still be safe. Even if you're busted, you should still be able to retrieve your personal wheels from the impound (and you absolutely should: sneaking into impounds is one of GTA 6's most satisfying activities).

Third, and arguably the most important: your car is a mobile wardrobe that can hold five outfits plus extra hats.

That's more crucial than it sounds because of how the police work in GTA 6. When you're clocked as a criminal, cops will have your description, but a new outfit, hat and sunglasses completely covers the scent of sin. You could buy some new clothes, of course, but you'll need a nearby clothes shop and some cash. It's easier and faster to grab some new gear from your trunk and drive off like nothing happened.

These three factors mean that when I have to dump my owned vehicle – changing cars to lose the police, for example – I feel vulnerable. Thankfully, it's easy to get it back by calling Joey in Chapter 1, or via the ScooterBros app, which you unlock later.

All these systems make me want to properly invest in my cars. In upgrades, yes, but also in mastering the act of driving them, learning their nuances and quirks. In GTA 5, Franklin's Bravado Buffalo S was just another vehicle to me, and I was constantly swapping between stolen cars to get from A to B, each handling differently. In GTA 6, I know exactly how much throttle Jason's Ganado pickup can take before it tailslides, and exactly the right angle for skidding around swampy corners without wrapping around a tendrilled tree.

And I take more care when weaving through traffic because crashing in GTA 6 peels off fenders and crumples bumpers faster than ever.

I'm deep into Chapter 2, but (mild spoiler alert!) I haven't even begun registering and storing new cars in garages. I've stolen and sold plenty – another new feature in GTA 6 – and will steal and sell plenty more. No doubt GTA 6's preoccupation with vehicles will continue, and I can't wait to see how cars change as the game unfolds.

If Red Dead Redemption 2 is the horse game, shrunken bollocks and all, then GTA 6 is without doubt the car game.

Samuel is a freelance reporter and editor specializing in longform journalism and hardware reviews. You can read his work at his website .

articles.title: American Psycho Remake From Director Luca Guadagnino No Longer Happening
articles.summary: Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.
articles.body:
Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.

The Challengers and Call Me by Your Name movie maker delivered the disappointing news when asked for an update on Deadline's Crew Call podcast. He admitted the script for the project that he read, which was penned by the writer behind The Bourne Ultimatum and Side Effects, was "fantastic" but not something he can continue working on.

"American Psycho, which is a fantastic script from Scott Z. Burns, unfortunately, is not happening for me, as we speak," Guadagnino said.

The Folio Society's American Psycho Illustrated Edition Image Gallery

Guadagnino has more than proven himself as a name capable of handling the weight of a property on the level of American Psycho, which is exactly why movie fans were so excited to hear he could be attached to the project in 2024. Although fans have referred to what would have become his slice into the well-established movie universe as a 'remake,' at the time of its announcement, Lionsgate teased that the project would have been more of an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' American Psycho novel, rather than a remake of Christian Bale's 2000 movie .

Updates on Guadagnino's American Psycho have been few and far between in the years since its announcement, though. Elvis star Austin Butler was once in the running for the role of Patrick Bateman, as was Euphoria's Jacob Elordi. It was reported in October 2025 that the film would not gender-swap its lead role .

Bale eventually went on to comment on Guadagnino's reimagining and another actor bringing his iconic character to the big screen. He said "all the best to 'em" just earlier this year, adding, "I like brave people."

The director didn't explain why his version of American Psycho won't be moving forward, just that it's "not happening for me." While that means any version of American Psycho won't be coming to movies anytime soon, it's unclear if Lionsgate has completely closed the door on Patrick Bateman. With Burns' script finished, there's always the chance a different filmmaker could take the reins.

For now, though, it's best to assume the American Psycho remake/adaptation is well and truly dead. In the meantime, Guadagnino is gearing up for the release of his Sam Altman biopic, Artificial . The film is gearing up for a limited premiere Christmas 2026 before getting a wider release January 8, 2027.

articles.title: Forget the Lighthouse, GTA 6’s Best Minigame Is a Full-Blown Zombie Shooter That Will Take You Hours To Beat
articles.summary: Yes, we know you're all playing GTA 6, but don't forget to check out Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, the certified banger on Jason's JoySystem console.
articles.body:
To say I was up until midnight last night with GTA 6 is technically correct, but not the full picture. What I was actually doing was headshotting undead nightmares in Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, a moreish isometric twin-stick shooter that lives inside Jason's PS5-alike JoySystem.

You play it briefly with Cal during the story, and it impressed me enough to want to beat it fully. After nearly four hours, I still haven't.

It's clearly inspired by the Sony-published Dead Nation from 2010, but it mashes the zombie slaying with a roguelike deckbuilder. Every time an enemy squelches, their blood splattering the pavement, you gain XP, and at each new level you pick a card to adjust your build. Basic cards boost movement speed, fire rate, damage or critical hit chance, but rarer cards transform your tactics, such as one that doubles your damage given and received.

Your goal is to collect six gears strewn around a deceptively large map and leave via a rooftop chopper. You'll die a lot, but on each run you'll learn a little more about the world's layout and discover new cards to experiment with.

The satisfaction of Street Trash 3 is in crafting a build on the fly from the cards you're dealt, and in feeling your power spiral. You're constantly levelling up and that escalation, the way your build rapidly grows and branches depending on what you find, reminds me a lot of Vampire Survivors . Like that game, it's most fun when you lean into a specific skill: the closest I've come to victory was when I swapped my pistol for a micro-SMG, buffing and buffing my fire rate until the bullets streamed like a deadly snake.

I also got deep on a run boosting my speed and stamina so I could infinitely sprint from groups of enemies, and another where – inspired by a detailed Reddit thread discussing the best builds – I found a card that improved my critical chance by 50% while standing still. When combined with other critical hit cards, I could basically stand in the same spot and mow down everything down around me, painting a gruesome circle of guts.

It is ludicrous that something as meaty and polished as Street Trash 3 exists inside another video game – and even more ludicrous that it's one of three games you can play on Jason's console (Rockstar told Kotaku that "an internal dev team within the dev team" makes these games).

But, like in real life, not every game available for the JoySystem is a banger. Of the three games on Jason’s hard drive, Time Jackers Rewind is the most forgettable. It's a stylish top-down shooter that plays a bit like a slower, sci-fi, less-good Hotline Miami . I appreciate how its checkpoints are tantalizingly spread far enough that you can't just sprint between them, close enough that after every death I was sure I was seconds away. Sadly its best weapon, a concussive shotgun that rumbles your controller, runs out of ammo after just a few seconds, and it's tricky to see enemies among all the on-screen effects.

Tenenbrae Lux is the third, a joke about auteurs stretched into an entire puzzle game. The developer is Johannes Zuch, a clear play on The Witness developer Jonathan Blow (Zuch/Suck, get it?), and his name is listed 38 times during the end credits, including as "architect as perception" and "left stick sensitivity tension consultant". This, surely, is a send-up of Hideo Kajima popping up multiple times in his own credits. The looping stairway in its central puzzle evokes Kojima's P.T. but if you squint you can also see riffs on Alan Wake, Dear Esther, and Robert Eggers’ black-and-white 2019 film The Lighthouse.

As a puzzler, it's intriguing. I say intriguing rather than fun because I can't say I really enjoyed it. The narrator's dialogue is deliberately grandiloquent and recondite ("Hark! An unearthly sound beckons. Like the sirens call, I am fated to find its source"), and the central puzzle is mind-bendingly complicated. Without completley spoiling it, you must loop through a series of rooms in a bunker and spot anomalies, cross-reference them with other clues to assign them a number, and then arrange those numbers in chronological order using a calendar in each room.

Rewarding when you've solved it, for sure, but a pain when you're trying.

The whole thing takes a couple of hours to complete, less if you look up the strategy guides than now exist across the internet (although note that the bunker puzzle is different for each player). And so if you want to beat all of the games on Jason's console, then, you'll need roughly five hours at the very least. That's a pretty impressive amount of game that's not Grand Theft Auto 6 in your copy of Grand Theft Auto 6.

What I love most about these three games is that they are entirely optional, like the majority of GTA 6. There is so much craft that most players simply won't see, so many developer hours spent creating missable moments of delight, so many systems I haven't yet engaged with. It speaks to both Rockstar's budget and its confidence, and as a player it's comforting to know that pretty much wherever I turn I'll find something hand-crafted and surprising. No matter how much time I put in, I couldn't possibly see everything.

What I can do, though, is see everything in Street Trash 3: Dezombifier. Back in I wade, for one more run.

articles.title: Rockstar Says Jason's Viral Personality in GTA 6 Comes From Steve McQueen and Real-Life Veterans
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.

As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval. Stoic, nonchalant, calm, composed, resigned; whatever you want to call one of GTA 6's new protagonists, Rockstar says it carefully crafted his already iconic demeanor by pulling from a Steve McQueen classic and real-life veterans.

The studio's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, talked about how the studio behind the mega-hit video game built Jason from the ground up during a conversation with Destructoid . Centering the story on a "couple on the run" marked new territory for Rockstar, but it's far from a new concept in entertainment. So, the team turned to movies, particularly Sam Peckinpah's The Getaway.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

"Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries explained. "We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."

He continued, saying that Rockstar's research into real-world veterans and Army Rangers helped refine its approach. Those who have played the game (and keen-eyed trailer watchers ) already know about Jason's military background, so the influence here definitely tracks.

"These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."

Jason is the talk of Vice City and has been for some time. As Rockstar shared more details about its seemingly shy lead ahead of GTA 6's launch, some fans began to wonder if he could be the franchise's first-ever neurodivergent protagonist . In addition to his personality, Humphries described Jason as "wired differently" during a recent interview with Love magazine.

While Jason steals more than just wads of cash in Vice City, his partner in crime has proven to be just as impactful. Game writer Michael Wiafe said looking into the kind of criminal activity known to make headlines in Florida was one of the first things the team did when creating both Jason and Lucia. For Rockstar, it wasn't just about creating true-to-life criminals; it was about creating fully realized human beings.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn’t stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What’s important is how they resonate, no matter where you’re experiencing the game in the world."

Between the chaos of robbing gas stations and drug dealers and getting into high-speed car chases, Jason and Lucia can become quite the power couple. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern said to Destructoid, "You really want them to make it." The quiet moments where the duo scrolls through social media in their bed or drives the other one to work can be just as important as the action set pieces. Gauvey-Kern added, "Those need to hit too, and you need to connect with how the characters are feeling in those moments."

Although GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S three days ago, Leonida is packed with enough things to do to keep players playing for months. While we wait to see what's next for Rockstar, you can check out IGN's 10/10 review . You can also read about how the developers made every NPC feel like real people you could run into on the street .

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. articles.title: Amazon and Target Launch '3 for 2' Sales on Books, Box Sets, and Vinyl for Black Friday
articles.body:
Target has officially launched its main Black Friday sale, which means Amazon is now matching all of the best deals in its own sale . This is especially good news for anyone looking to pad their book or vinyl collections this year thanks to the popular '3 for 2' sale returning at both major retailers ahead of Thanksgiving.

This is actually the second time the two retailers have had this type of sale in November, but this time around there seems to be a lot more included here. That's especially true if you're looking to grab multiple box sets at a discount. This sale is arguably the best time to buy books at a discount if you're willing to spend a bit more to get the extra savings.

Buy 2, Get 1 Free Sale on Books and Music

For those who aren't already familiar with this sale, the way it works is pretty easy to understand. All you need to do is add three eligible items to your cart and the least expensive one will get discounted from the price at check out. Because of this, you'll want to buy three similarly priced items to maximize the discount you're getting. You can also mix and match anything in the sale, so you don't need to just buy three books or three vinyl records.

The Lord of the Rings Deluxe Illustrated Edition

Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince: The Illustrated Edition

I Spy Christmas: A Book of Picture Riddles

The book portion of this sale is quite massive, so it's definitely worth diving into all of the book inclusions to see what's there. If you're looking for some recommendations on where to get started, however, I've picked out some of the most interesting titles I could find.

The Dungeon Crawler Carl books on sale here are always incredibly popular during these sales. Matt Dinniman's LitRPG series has really blown up this year and it's a great opportunity to pick up the full collection for pretty cheap. It's also worth checking out Pierce Brown's Red Rising series , which has been hitting the zeitgeist again after the movie adaptation news earlier this year . And if you're into romantasy, Sarah J. Maas' latest ACOTAR book is even included here.

If you're just looking for some cool stuff to add to your shelf, I'd recommend checking out Hyrule Historia first. This is an art book that details the long and interesting Legend of Zelda history. There are also illustrated versions of Lord of the Rings and Harry Potter included here this year.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians 5 Book Paperback Boxed Set

George R. R. Martin's A Game of Thrones 5-Book Boxed Set

A Court of Thorns and Roses Hardcover Box Set

Frank Herbert's Dune Saga 3-Book Boxed Set

The box sets included in the sale are the best overall deal for anyone looking to start their book collection. These are higher-priced items that include either all of the books in a series or a good chunk of them at once. They will often also feature some sort of cool artwork on the spines that look wonderful together on your shelf.

As for what you should check out first, I recommend grabbing The Witcher books on sale here. These books spawned one of the most successful video game franchises of all time and, according to the author , will still be getting new stories. I'd recommend the Game of Thrones box set for similar reasons, but George R.R. Martin may never finish that series so dive into those books at your own risk.

There are also some great fantasy box sets that have since been turned into movies or TV shows. The Hunger Games box set includes the latest prequel, Sunrise on the Reaping, which is now in theaters. There's also the Percy Jackson books , which is worth reading alongside season 3 of the Disney+ adaptation . And if you don't already own all of the Harry Potter books , the paperback set is definitely worth grabbing ahead of HBO's TV show next month.

The sale on music is just as robust as the book selection. So although I've picked out some of the things I personally think are cool, I encourage you to check out the full inclusion list for yourself and search for albums you know you like.

That being said, my overall top pick in the sale is the Lord of the Rings trilogy. Howard Shore's music helped turn Peter Jackson's movies into something truly epic. This is an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a good LOTR gift to buy someone this year.

A few of my other top picks include classics like Michael Jackson's Thriller, Metallica's Master of Puppets, and the Beatle's Abby Road. Noah Khan's Stick Season is also included here as it's been one of the most popular albums of the last few years.

With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .
